sources.title: o1 API model reference
sources.evidence: Reopened the exact o1 Markdown reference from its successful October 27 HTTP 200 fetch. The o1 alias identifies o1-2024-12-17 and is marked shut down. Last-documented specifications are 200,000 context, 100,000 output, text/image input, text output, reasoning and function calling. Exact cached-input pricing establishes o1 caching support. The complete reference supplies neither total nor active parameter counts.

sources.title: Introducing ChatGPT Pro — December 5, 2024
sources.evidence: Dated first-party announcement offers full OpenAI o1 in ChatGPT on December 5. It separately describes o1 pro mode; this report audits ordinary o1, not the preview or pro mode.

sources.title: OpenAI o1 and new tools for developers
sources.evidence: Freshly reopened October 27. Explicitly calls o1-2024-12-17 a new post-trained version of the model released in ChatGPT two weeks earlier. Documents function calling, structured outputs, developer messages, vision and reasoning-effort control. This is explicit lineage, but neither checkpoint has a published nominal parameter count here to inherit. API rollout initially targets usage tier 5.

sources.title: OpenAI API changelog
sources.evidence: December 17, 2024 entry releases full o1 in the API with function calling, developer messages, structured outputs, vision and reasoning-effort control. The September release instead names o1-preview and o1-mini; neither replaces the December 5 full-o1 public release date.

sources.title: OpenAI o1 System Card
sources.evidence: Reopened the full 52-page PDF from its successful October 27 HTTP 200 fetch and searched its complete text for parameter counts. Sections 2-3 describe training, distinguish near-final and December 5 checkpoints, and explicitly say their incremental post-training improvements kept the same base model. A footnote excludes the December 17 update. No nominal total or active count for the model or its base is supplied.

sources.title: OpenAI GPT-4.5 System Card — February 27, 2025
sources.evidence: Reopened the full later report from its successful October 27 HTTP 200 fetch. Tables 1-4 and the other exact o1 comparisons report safety, refusal, hallucination and capability metrics. A complete-text parameter/architecture search found no total or active o1 count; API sampling parameters are not model-size disclosures.

sources.title: gpt-oss-120b & gpt-oss-20b Model Card
sources.evidence: Reopened the full later report from its successful October 27 HTTP 200 fetch. Section 2/Table 1 give explicit total and active counts only for the gpt-oss checkpoints. Figure 4 compares HealthBench with exact o1 and calls gpt-oss-20b significantly smaller, but gives no numerical o1 total or active count. Similar training or comparative performance does not establish named base-model lineage.

sources.title: Deliberative Alignment: Reasoning Enables Safer Language Models
sources.evidence: Reopened the full paper from its successful October 27 HTTP 200 fetch. Sections 2.3.3-2.4 describe SFT and RL, including the reward signal used for o1 and o3-mini; Table 1 explicitly compares exact o1 safety metrics. Complete-text parameter/architecture search found no nominal production total or active count and no counted base model.

sources.title: Prompt Caching 201
sources.evidence: Archived recipe explicitly scopes itself to models before GPT-5.6 and explains OpenAI prompt caching as reuse of key/value projections in Transformer attention layers. Combined with exact o1 cached-input pricing and its 2024 release, this supports only a qualified broad Transformer inference, not dense/MoE structure or a size.

sources.title: Learning Powerful Models: From Transformers to Reasoners and Beyond
sources.evidence: Read the public OpenAI research presentation transcript. It discusses Transformer priors and reasoning models and compares o1 results, but says reasoning models are usually Transformers rather than specifying an exact o1 topology. Its hypothetical scaling counts are not o1 production parameters.

sources.title: File inputs
sources.evidence: For vision-capable models, PDF inputs are processed into extracted text and page images. This supports PDF as a documented API input format alongside native text/image input; it is not an independent neural modality or evidence of a live retired endpoint.

sources.title: OpenAI API deprecations
sources.evidence: April 22, 2026 announcement explicitly identifies o1 and o1-2024-12-17; access shut down October 23, 2026. Specifications are preserved as last-documented capabilities, with no claim that requests still succeed.

sources.title: OpenAI Services Agreement
sources.evidence: Sections 2.2 and 9.1 provide limited API/service-use rights and reserve service intellectual property. Together with the hosted product/API release, this supports a descriptive Proprietary classification rather than an open-weight license.

sources.title: All OpenAI models
sources.evidence: Official catalog identifies o1 as a shut-down reasoning model and separately lists the Apache-licensed gpt-oss open-weight models. No o1 checkpoint distribution is listed.

sources.title: EU AI Act: OpenAI Resources and Customer Guidance
sources.evidence: Checked the published training-summary index; it has no exact o1 summary. Summaries for newer GPT models were not transferred to o1.

sources.title: Models.dev o1 record
sources.evidence: Read the upstream lead independently. It provides the December 5 release, broad o-family label, context and capability flags, but no parameter evidence. Primary releases and technical sources were used for verification.

sources.title: Attempted later o3-mini system card
sources.evidence: Direct web fetch returned 404. This unavailable document is not used to establish any field; accessible later GPT-4.5 and gpt-oss reports were inspected instead.

sources.title: DeepSeek-R1: Incentivizing Reasoning Capability in LLMs via Reinforcement Learning
sources.evidence: Freshly reopened October 27. Original model-team Table 4 explicitly separates # Activated Params and # Total Params; both cells for OpenAI o1-1217 are dashes. The Baselines paragraph identifies this December API model and says its performance comes from official reports. This exact-snapshot comparison supplies no nominal count; the 37B/671B values belong to DeepSeek models.

sources.title: Qwen3 Technical Report
sources.evidence: Freshly reopened October 27. Original model-team Table 11 compares OpenAI-o1 and explicitly labels # Activated Params and # Total Params; both o1 cells are dashes. Section 4.6 identifies o1 as a reasoning baseline, without a snapshot suffix. The table establishes no o1 count and is not an OpenAI architecture disclosure.

sources.title: Can Large Reasoning Models Reason about Spatial Relations?
sources.evidence: Freshly opened the author-hosted full paper October 27, then downloaded and visually inspected Table 1 on PDF page 4. Its exact o1-2024-12-17-high row says Number of Parameters: Undisclosed, while DeepSeek separately has total and activated counts. This original empirical research corroborates the unresolved size of the evaluated o1 snapshot; it is not an exhaustive disclosure search or an OpenAI specification.

name.note: Exact ordinary full-model name; distinguish o1-preview, o1-mini and o1 pro mode.

family.note: The exact reference and system card explicitly identify the o1 model family; use this more specific family within the broader o-series.

release_date.note: Earliest public full-o1 release in ChatGPT. The December 17 API snapshot is a later post-trained revision; September o1-preview is a different model.

open_weights.note: Released through proprietary hosted products and API; no public o1 weight distribution is documented. Open-weight gpt-oss is explicitly separate.

license.note: Descriptive licensing classification based on limited hosted-service rights; not an SPDX weight license.

parameters_b.note: Fresh October 27 searches and reopened original sources found no supported nominal total. The original card and December API release document unchanged-base/post-training relationships, but no counted base to inherit. DeepSeek-R1 Table 4 and Qwen3 Table 11 leave total o1 parameters blank; GeoAI Table 1 calls the exact December snapshot undisclosed. The later gpt-oss size comparison is qualitative.

active_parameters_b.note: Rechecked independently of total size. Later original model-team comparisons explicitly provide activated-parameter rows but leave o1 blank: DeepSeek-R1 Table 4 (o1-1217) and Qwen3 Table 11 (OpenAI-o1). No active count, counted-base convention or routing disclosure was found in the reopened OpenAI sources. Neither a broad Transformer inference nor gpt-oss counts establish o1 active parameters.

architecture.note: Qualified broad inference: exact o1 cached-input pricing binds it to prompt caching, and the applicable pre-GPT-5.6 engineering recipe describes Transformer attention and KV reuse. This is not an exact o1 architecture specification; layer count, dense versus MoE structure and multimodal component topology remain undisclosed. Training research and the general reasoning-model talk do not justify more detail.

context_window.note: Last-documented API context for default o1-2024-12-17; maximum output is separately 100,000 tokens. This is not a claim that the original December 5 ChatGPT product exposed the same context or that the retired API still operates.

modalities.note: Native text/image input and text output. PDF is retained as an API file format converted to text and page images. No native audio/video support is claimed; API capabilities are last documented after shutdown.

reasoning.note: Explicit reinforcement-learning-based reasoning and internal chain of thought; API revision supports configurable reasoning effort.

tool_call.note: Function calling explicitly introduced for the December 17 API revision and retained in the last-documented reference. Do not retroactively attribute all API tools to December 5 ChatGPT or claim a currently live endpoint.

description.value: Reasoning model for complex tasks with text and image input and support for function calling.
description.note: Plain description of documented capabilities; release/revision and retirement qualifications are kept in notes.

patch.notes: Full o1 first released in ChatGPT on December 5, 2024. The API default o1-2024-12-17 is a later post-trained revision with function calling and vision; its last-documented context is 200,000 tokens with 100,000 maximum output. OpenAI shut down o1 and that API snapshot on October 23, 2026. PDF input is converted to text and page images. Broad Transformer architecture is inferred from exact-model caching support and the applicable pre-GPT-5.6 engineering explanation; detailed topology remains undisclosed. Total and active parameter counts remain undisclosed; the documented December post-training lineage supplies no nominal size.

summary: October 27 parameter-only re-audit retains null/undisclosed total and active counts after fresh searches, reopened OpenAI sources and later original DeepSeek-R1, Qwen3 and GeoAI comparison tables. Explicit post-training lineage was evaluated but has no published counted base. Add explicit null parameter patches and parameters_source; preserve the other 12 assessments, including the December release/revision distinction and last-documented capabilities after shutdown.
